objective: Promote the already accepted embodied core revision into one visually production-ready Godot encounter. Re-verify the accepted core with factory-owned shipping-input evidence, approve coherent whole-scene targets derived from that live scene, activate only the asset lanes required by the selected target, integrate production assets and state-linked motion, then refresh trusted runtime evidence before multimodal and Sol judgment. Use a separate tournament campaign only for a named unresolved fork. Do not rebuild the core game, present proxy state logic, use static scene plates as runtime worlds, or describe concept art, generated source, extracted source, or engine-ready assets as production.

nodes.instructions: Re-run the factory-owned Godot probe against the promoted core revision before visual work begins. Fail closed if shipping input, visible movement, spatial interaction, state consequence, or continuous engine evidence no longer matches the accepted slice contract. Write only factory evidence and do not modify the game. This is the immutable production baseline; the separate post-integration evidence node refreshes after writer repairs.

Starting from the accepted core revision and its fresh factory-owned shipping-camera evidence, define one feasible engine-native visual system and create multiple coherent whole-screen targets for the representative encounter. Specify rendering grid, palette, typography roles, sprite and animation contracts, peer layout regions, UI surface families, anti-patterns, and controlled scene life. Preserve the proven navigable space, actor scale, interactive entity positions, controls, and causal sequence across interaction, action, feedback, and resolution states. Treat generated screens as art-direction references, never runtime plates. The component map must separate environment layers, player/NPC actors, interactive props, effects, and UI into independently animatable runtime consumers. Write the design-system handoff and a valid gamefactory.scene-target/v1 manifest, leave production absent, and return revise if no direction can be faithfully decomposed into the live scene.

Review every proposed full-scene target at the shipping camera before component production begins. Verify actual gameplay, interaction hierarchy, required states, text zones, relative scale, navigation, and engine feasibility. Audit the declared peer regions across every state; reject accidental overlaps, clipped copy, competing layers, or decorative frames that obscure controls or actors. Audit typography as an information system and reject tiny or overused pixel type when it weakens hierarchy or sustained reading. Review the motion plan for controlled life: ambient continuity, interaction response, gameplay consequence, and state transition should be appropriate and mutually coherent, without requiring constant motion. Reject concept art, nonsensical controls, frozen tableaux, decorative clutter, inconsistent scale, or a target that cannot be decomposed. Return pass only with one approved target id and hash, approved state variants, experience contract, and component map; otherwise return revise with prioritized scene-level changes. On pass, the structured result MUST use this exact shape at minimum: {"outcome":"pass","summary":"...","findings":{"selectedTargetId":"...","selectedTargetSha256":"64 lowercase hex characters"}}. Do not nest selectedTargetId or selectedTargetSha256 under approval or another object.

Record the passed scene-target-gate decision without changing its creative work. Read the gate's selected target id, selected primary-view hash, and findings. Atomically bind the decision into both design/scene-targets/scene-target.json and design/scene-targets/validation.json when that validation manifest exists. In scene-target.json update only approval: status approved, reviewer scene-target-gate, selectedTargetSha256 equal to the gate-approved primary-view hash, findings copied from the review, and approvedAt as the current ISO timestamp. In validation.json mirror status, reviewer, selectedTargetId, selectedTargetSha256, and the identical approvedAt without changing measured checks. Validate scene-target.json as gamefactory.scene-target/v1 and fail if either manifest disagrees with the gate, selected view, or each other. Do not alter candidates, prompts, geometry, component maps, hashes, assets, or non-approval validation results.

Choose the smallest production method that can faithfully realize the approved scene target. Preserve creative latitude: return exactly one outcome from direct, segment, motion_study, pixel_motion, or segment_pixel_motion. Use direct for code-native work or assets that need neither segmentation nor generated motion. Use segment only when approved whole-scene imagery should be decomposed with SAM 3. Use motion_study only when an external generated video is useful as non-runtime motion reference. Use pixel_motion when a generated motion study should be tracked and compiled into palette-locked runtime frames; add segmentation only when static scene components also need extraction. Before selecting a provider lane, verify its configured request path and prerequisites are available; never select a paid or credentialed provider merely because it exists. Write design/asset-lanes/decision.json with rationale, selected outcome, required components, source scene ids and hashes, and expected outputs. For every selected lane, also write its valid candidate-local request: sam3.request.json, video.request.json, sam3.video.request.json, and/or pixel-motion.request.json. Pin the approved scene images as references and choose contained output directories. Do not generate or integrate assets in this node.

Promote exactly the accepted embodied encounter into a coherent production slice derived from the approved gamefactory.scene-target/v1 target, experience contract, and state variants. Preserve the already passing shipping input, spatial interaction, collision, camera, and causal loop; do not redesign or rebuild the core. Keep environment, player/NPC actors, interactive props, effects, and UI as independently rendered runtime consumers. Consume only the asset lanes selected by asset-lane-planner and distinguish skipped, failed, and usable outputs. Preserve target geometry, peer-region ownership, typography roles, component footprints, and target-hash lineage. Implement the motion plan as a living scene with locomotion, immediate interaction response, readable gameplay consequence, and transitions between important states. Produce the configured current runtime captures and return every runtime source file named by the accepted production inventory as a structured artifact. Do not claim that candidate-authored captures are trusted; the following factory-owned Godot node will establish current causal evidence. If any runtime surface remains provisional, return revise or visual-prototype instead of overstating maturity.

After every production integration or repair, rerun the factory-owned Godot import, shipping-input scenarios, causal trace, and continuous engine-frame capture. This evidence supersedes the pre-production baseline for all downstream reviews. Write only factory evidence; never repair the game or trust candidate-authored proof claims.

Independently audit the post-integration factory-owned shipping-camera frames and causal trace together with the approved scene target and configured production captures. Return revise for blocker or major hierarchy, overlap, scaling, typography, style-consistency, target-fidelity, motion-feedback, scene-life, or embodied-regression defects. Classify each finding as implementation, target, or spec ownership; prescribe the smallest coherent repair and do not send target or spec contradictions through endless implementation churn.

Make the final production-slice decision from the authoritative projectSlice contract, the accepted core revision, post-integration factory-owned Godot evidence, approved whole-scene target, Gemini multimodal findings, deterministic design-system checks, asset maturity, and polish manifest. Recompute runtime hashes and verify that every accepted production-inventory output is present in the production-slice-builder's structured artifact list. Return pass only if shipping input still produces visible actor motion and spatial consequence, every required surface is production, every runtime component remains independently rendered and traceable to the selected scene target, and no blocker, runtime placeholder, compile-only bootstrap, or monolithic interactive scene plate remains. Treat implementation findings as bounded repairs; if the approved target is incoherent return a target-revision disposition, and if runtime evidence falsifies a consumed frozen claim return a spec-amendment disposition with claim IDs and preserved evidence. On pass, include projectEvidence in the structured output: each required scenario as {id, artifactSha256}, interactionTrace, embodiedGameplay, engineCapture, targetSha256, motionEvidence, and each required runtime asset as {id, consumer, artifactSha256}; every hash must identify an actual declared preserved artifact. Never call the game fun without human evidence.
